verdict.m118_p0_closed_scope: Commercial VCS closes reset-free directed mapper-to-accumulator conservation only when consecutive accepted events do not target the same accumulator address.

P0.title: Consecutive same-address services are accepted before downstream rejection
P0.evidence: M119 treats the output slot as available when M118 update_ready is high for the current token. The second service is accepted while the first same-address update enters M118. One cycle later M118 detects same_address_rdw_hazard, raises protocol_error and rejects the already accepted second update. Independent VCS observes 2 accepted events, 1 mapped update and 1 accumulator write.
P0.required_fix: Propagate a same-address interlock into service_ready, retain/retry the buffered mapper update until safe, or implement correct same-address forwarding. Re-run the identical independent attack and require 2 accepted == 2 mapped == 2 written without fault.

P0.title: Full accepted-transaction exact-once remains undefined for retry and reset
P0.evidence: A separated A-B-A retry is silently applied twice because no transaction identity/dedup exists. Reset after acceptance discards the pending event. These may be legal architectural choices, but M117-to-M120 replay/recovery semantics are not specified or verified, so the broad exact-once P0 cannot close.
P0.required_fix: Specify reset abort boundaries and retry ownership, add sequence identity or prove upstream no-retry behavior, then replay heldout M117 schedules with duplicate/retry/reset injections.

P1.title: Production directed test has no same-address consecutive event
P1.impact: The 1024/1024/1024 production ledger is true only for its address pattern and misses the integration hazard.

P1.title: M117 scheduler and heldout trace replay remain absent
P1.impact: No executable scheduled cycle ratio can be admitted from this island.

P1.title: Weight and accumulator memories are behavioral models
P1.impact: 700416 and 725416 bytes are logical geometry, not macro area, energy or timing.

P1.title: No macro-inclusive DC/PTPX/STA evidence exists
P1.impact: The island has no physical speedup, energy-efficiency or area claim.

P1.title: The exact-once property is simulation-directed rather than exhaustive
P1.impact: The production SVA checks next-cycle event-to-update mapping, but coverage does not establish all address, retry, reset and fault histories.

P2.title: Protocol error attribution is collapsed
P2.recommendation: Expose wrapper, mapper and accumulator fault causes for debug and recovery policy.

P2.title: Sparse windows still commit all 3072 vectors
P2.recommendation: Evaluate a valid-row commit bitmap or sparse drain only after exact-once is fixed; count metadata and ordering cost.

P2.title: Reset behavior lacks an explicit epoch/abort receipt
P2.recommendation: Expose an abort acknowledgement or epoch tag so upstream can distinguish discarded and committed accepted work.

safe_claim: Exact-SHA commercial VCS validates the frozen M120 island for two reset-free directed windows with 1024 accepted distinct-consecutive-address events, 1024 mapped updates, 1024 accumulator writes and 589824 checked commit lanes. It does not validate full accepted-transaction exact-once, foundry SRAM, scheduled cycle ratio, physical speedup or system speedup.
prohibited_claims: Do not generalize directed distinct-address conservation to consecutive same-address events.
Do not claim retry deduplication or reset recovery.
Do not call logical bytes foundry SRAM area or energy.
Do not promote the M109 2.53546204172554 projection to RTL, physical, system or headline speedup.
